title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: GAR 3 / PLAC — latitudo mortis; Caeterum tip before Caput V
pass_a_gloss: GAR. 3. No reason can be said why the name of death should not be taken in its whole latitude in this place; but that the name of death in the Scriptures is referred not only to the body but also to the soul and to spiritual things is plain from frequent testimonies of Scripture. See Ezekiel 3:18, Hosea 13:1, Matthew 8:22, Luke 9:60 and 15:24, Ephesians 2:1, 1 Timothy 5:6, Revelation 3:1, etc. PLAC. The reason is ready at hand, because spiritual death is sin, but not properly speaking the penalty of sin. But the Law threatens not sin, but only the properly so-called penalty of sin. But as for what he says, that authorities of grave men are not wanting, neither are authorities of men no less grave wanting to me also, and I already above praised the Helvetic Confession article 8. But what need is there to fight with human testimonies where reasons are present far stronger than they? For the rest you see what follows from this: for if the privation of righteousness is not a penalty denounced by the law, certainly it is not a penalty properly so called. Wherefore that actual sin of Adam is not to be ascribed to us by a vindicator of justice who imputes it.
pass_b_english: GAR. 3. No reason can be given why 'death' should not be taken here in its full breadth; and Scripture plainly refers the name of death not only to the body but also to the soul and to spiritual things—see Ezekiel 3:18; Hosea 13:1; Matthew 8:22; Luke 9:60 and 15:24; Ephesians 2:1; 1 Timothy 5:6; Revelation 3:1, and so on.

PLAC. The reason is ready: spiritual death is sin, not—properly speaking—the penalty of sin. The Law threatens not sin, but only the penalty of sin properly so called. As for authorities of weighty men not being wanting—authorities of men no less weighty are not wanting to me either, and I already cited the Helvetic Confession, article 8. But why fight with human witnesses where far stronger reasons are at hand? For the rest, see what follows: if privation of righteousness is not a penalty the law denounced, it is certainly not a penalty properly so called. Therefore that actual sin of Adam is not to be ascribed to us by justice's avenger as He imputes it.
source_text: GAR. 3. Nulla ratio dici potest, quare non mortis nomen in tota sua latitudine hoc loco sumatur; atqui mortis nomen in Scripturis non ad corpus modo, sed & ad animam, & spiritualia referri patet ex frequentibus Scripturae testimoniis. Vide Ezech. 3. 18. Os. 13. 1. Matth. 8. 22. Luc. 9. 60. & 15. 24. Ephes. 2. 1. 1. Tim. 5. 6. Apoc. 3. 1. &c. PLAC. Ratio est in promptu, quia mors spiritualis est peccatum, non autem proprie loquendo peccati poena. Comminatur autem Lex non peccatum, sed proprie dictam duntaxat peccati poenam. Quod autem ait, non deesse auctoritates gravium virorum, nec desunt etiam mihi non minus gravium virorum auctoritates, & jam supra Helveticam laudavi confessionem Art. 8. Sed quid opus est humanis pugnare testimoniis, ubi rationes adsunt illis multo validiores? Caeterum vides quid hinc sequatur: nam si privatio justitiae non est poena lege denunciata, certe poena proprie dicta non est. Quare non est adscribenda justitiae vindici nobis peccatum illud actuale Adami imputantis.
